newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX hits third high amid profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX hits third high amid profit-taking.

text.p: Hungarian share prices continued their bull run on Wednesday but traders said early gains were trimmed as certain investors decided to cash in profits towards the close of trade.
The BUX index finished at 5,815.38 points, up 128.69.
"The trend seemed to reverse within the session due to intraday profit-taking," one trader said.

Traders said the market was driven by domestic corporate news and expectations of good corporate results rather than by an almost unanimous market prediction that the U.S. Fed will leave its rates steady.

"I think the market takes it for sure that (rates will remain unchanged)...thus corporate news and expectations of corporate results moved the market," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
Several stocks soared to new record levels before retreating.
Oil company MOL shares surged to 3,790 forints then slid to close at 3,625 forints, up 30.
"MOL, along with (pharmaceuticals) Richter and OTP Bank is rising mainly because the market still thinks it is relatively cheap," one trader said earlier today.
Keresztesi said speculation ahead of the pricing of MOL shares for the upcoming phase of its privatisation and expectations of good annual results were among the factors moving MOL's price.
Richter's price was bolstered also by news that Germany's Linde won a contract to build a new 100 million mark pharmaceutical plant for Richter.
"The news of the plant gave a big boost to Richter's price," one trader said earlier today. "The news had a beneficial impact but the whole market is going upward," another said.
Richter also came down from its new record level of 11,950 forints to close at 11,810, up 415.
Elsewhere on the market chemicals stocks closed lower while bank stocks were mixed.
Borsodchem closed at 6,195 forints, down 55 from Tuesday and sharply below the day's peak of 6,500. TVK slipped 40 forints to end at 2,580, below the day's high of 2,670.
OTP Bank finished at 3,750, up 150 from yesterday, while Inter-Europa Bank closed at 50,000, down 1,400.
Garment factory Styl was suspended for the whole day after a daily newspaper released information about the company's 1996 results and 1997 plans.
"There's a possibility that market participants do not have equal access to the information," the bourse explained.
Holding company Skala-Coop was also suspended after a too rapid intraday rise of over 20 percent.
